views.name: job_postings_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  jf.job_id,
  jf.company_id,
  jf.job_title_short,
  jf.job_title,
  jf.job_location,
  jf.job_via,
  jf.job_schedule_type,
  jf.job_work_from_home,
  jf.search_location,
  jf.job_posted_date,
  jf.job_no_degree_mention,
  jf.job_health_insurance,
  jf.job_country,
  jf.salary_rate,
  jf.salary_year_avg,
  jf.salary_hour_avg,
  jc.name AS name,
  jc.link AS link,
  jc.link_google AS link_google,
  jc.thumbnail AS thumbnail,
  sj.skill_id AS skill_id
FROM job_postings_fact AS jf
LEFT JOIN job_company AS jc
  ON jf.company_id = jc.company_id
LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim AS sj
  ON jf.job_id = sj.job_id
views.description: Denormalized row per job posting enriched with company and associated skill ids. Use this when analyzing job-level measures together with company metadata or skill associations. This preserves one row per job_id; if multiple skills exist per job this will produce multiple rows (one per skill association). | Use for: Job counts or salary averages by company, location, or skill; Join job postings to company metadata; Analyze distribution of job attributes for postings that list particular skills (after joining to skills_dim)
counter_examples: Among job postings that specifically have the Data Analyst, require a non-null annual average salary, and are remote, what is the overall average salary when considering only the top three most frequently demanded skills for these positions?

views.name: job_postings_company_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  company_id,
  COUNT(*) AS job_postings_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_work_from_home = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS work_from_home_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_no_degree_mention = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_degree_mention_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN job_health_insurance = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS health_insurance_count,
  AVG(salary_year_avg) AS avg_salary_year,
  AVG(salary_hour_avg) AS avg_salary_hour
FROM job_postings_fact
GROUP BY company_id
views.description: Aggregated metrics per company (one row per company_id) summarizing job posting counts and salary statistics. Use for company-level reporting and comparisons. This preserves company_id as the key. | Use for: Rank or compare companies by number of job postings; Correlate company-level average salary with prevalence of remote work or benefits mentions; Create dashboards showing company hiring activity

views.name: skills_with_type
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  skill_id,
  skills,
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(type) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE type
  END AS type
FROM skills_dim
views.description: Canonical skill dimension projection: one row per skill_id with skill text and type normalized to NULL when blank. Use when you need a clean skills lookup before joining to job associations. | Use for: Lookup skill names or filter jobs by skill type; Aggregate jobs by skill categories after joining skills_job_dim
counter_examples: Among job postings that specifically have the Data Analyst, require a non-null annual average salary, and are remote, what is the overall average salary when considering only the top three most frequently demanded skills for these positions?

views.name: alien_profile_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id,
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  a.email,
  a.gender,
  a.type,
  a.birth_year,
  ad.age AS age,
  ad.favorite_food AS favorite_food,
  ad.feeding_frequency AS feeding_frequency,
  ad.aggressive AS aggressive,
  al.current_location AS current_location,
  al.state AS state,
  al.country AS country,
  al.occupation AS occupation
FROM aliens AS a
LEFT JOIN alien_data AS ad
  ON a.id = ad.id
LEFT JOIN aliens_location AS al
  ON ad.current_location = al.current_location
views.description: Denormalized alien profile combining core identity, location and detail attributes. One row per alien id. Useful for people-level analyses without needing to join separate tables each time. Preserves identity columns from aliens and denormalized attributes from related tables when available via left joins. | Use for: Profile aliens by location, age, or aggressive flag; Count aliens by country or occupation; Identify mismatches between denormalized alien_data and normalized aliens/aliens_location tables

views.name: cities_country_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.city_id,
  c.city_name,
  c.latitude,
  c.longitude,
  c.country_code_2,
  c.capital,
  c.population,
  c.insert_date,
  cc.country_id AS country_id,
  cc.country_name AS country_name,
  cc.country_code_3 AS country_code_3,
  cc.region AS region,
  cc.sub_region AS sub_region,
  cc.intermediate_region AS intermediate_region,
  cc.created_on AS created_on
FROM cities AS c
LEFT JOIN cities_countries AS cc
  ON LOWER(c.country_code_2) = LOWER(cc.country_code_2)
views.description: One row per city joined to its country metadata by country_code_2. Use for geolocation analyses combining city-level population/coordinates with country-level attributes. | Use for: Aggregate city populations by country or region; Map jobs or aliens to country/region via city; Filter capital cities and their country attributes
counter_examples: Identify the country with data inserted on nine different days in January 2022. Then, find the longest consecutive period with data insertions for this country during January 2022, and calculate the proportion of entries that are from its capital city within this longest consecutive insertion period.

views.name: legislator_latest_term
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  lt.id_bioguide,
  lt.term_number,
  lt.term_id,
  lt.term_type,
  lt.term_start,
  lt.term_end,
  lt.state,
  lt.district,
  lt.class,
  lt.party,
  lt.how,
  lt.url,
  lt.address,
  lt.phone,
  lt.fax,
  lt.contact_form,
  lt.office,
  lt.state_rank,
  lt.rss_url,
  lt.caucus
FROM (
  SELECT *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id_bioguide ORDER BY COALESCE(term_end, term_start) DESC) AS rn
  FROM legislators_terms
) AS lt
WHERE lt.rn = 1
views.description: Latest term per legislator id_bioguide based on term_end date. One row per id_bioguide representing the most recent term record. Useful for retrieving current state/district/party information. | Use for: Get current party/state/district for each legislator; Join latest term info back to legislator bio table

views.name: legislators_person
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.full_name,
  l.first_name,
  l.last_name,
  l.middle_name,
  l.nickname,
  l.suffix,
  l.other_names_end,
  l.other_names_middle,
  l.other_names_last,
  l.birthday,
  l.gender,
  l.id_bioguide,
  l.id_bioguide_previous_0,
  l.id_govtrack,
  l.id_icpsr,
  l.id_wikipedia,
  l.id_wikidata,
  l.id_google_entity_id,
  l.id_house_history,
  l.id_house_history_alternate,
  l.id_thomas,
  l.id_cspan,
  l.id_votesmart,
  l.id_lis,
  l.id_ballotpedia,
  l.id_opensecrets,
  l.id_fec_0,
  l.id_fec_1,
  l.id_fec_2,
  lt.term_id AS term_id,
  lt.term_start AS term_start,
  lt.term_end AS term_end,
  lt.state AS state,
  lt.district AS district,
  lt.party AS party
FROM legislators AS l
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id_bioguide ORDER BY COALESCE(term_end, term_start) DESC) AS rn
    FROM legislators_terms
  ) WHERE rn = 1
) AS lt
  ON l.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
views.description: One row per legislator (from legislators) with their latest term attributes joined in. Use for combined person+office analyses while preserving legislator identity columns. | Use for: List current legislators with contact/office info; Analyze legislator demographics by party or state

views.name: cities_cn_july_insert_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  city_name,
  country_code_2,
  insert_date
FROM cities
WHERE country_code_2 = 'cn'
  AND insert_date >= '2021-07-01'
  AND insert_date <= '2021-07-31'
views.description: Subset of city rows for cities in China (country_code_2 = 'cn') that have an insert_date present in the July 2021 month. This is a filtered cohort used as the base set of dated city observations.

views.name: cities_insert_date_dedup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.insert_date AS insert_date,
  c.city_id AS city_id,
  c.city_name AS city_name
FROM cities c
JOIN (
  SELECT insert_date, MIN(city_id) AS min_city_id
  FROM cities
  WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY insert_date
) d ON d.insert_date = c.insert_date AND d.min_city_id = c.city_id
views.description: One row per insert_date representing a single chosen city for that date from the provided date-filtered city rows. If multiple cities share the same insert_date, pick one deterministically (e.g., lowest city_id). Produces a canonical daily series of city rows for days that have at least one city record.

views.name: streak_length_extremes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- generate a distinct streak id per contiguous run of city insert_date values per city_name
  (city_name || '|' || MIN(insert_date) || '|' || MAX(insert_date)) AS streak_id,
  MIN(insert_date) AS streak_start_date,
  MAX(insert_date) AS streak_end_date,
  CAST((julianday(MAX(insert_date)) - julianday(MIN(insert_date)) + 1) AS INTEGER) AS streak_length
FROM (
  SELECT
    city_id,
    city_name,
    insert_date,
    -- rank rows per city by date to detect contiguous runs
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city_name ORDER BY insert_date) AS rn,
    -- convert date to julian integer to allow gap-based grouping
    CAST(julianday(insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS jd
  FROM cities
  WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
)
-- streak grouping: for contiguous calendar-day runs, grouping key = jd - rn
GROUP BY city_name, (jd - rn)
views.description: Aggregate distinct streaks to produce their lengths and identify extreme streak lengths (minimum positive streak_length and maximum streak_length) among the set of streaks derived from the date-filtered city rows.

views.name: cities_june_2022_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  country_code_2,
  date(insert_date) AS insert_date_date
FROM
  cities
WHERE
  date(insert_date) >= '2022-06-01'
  AND date(insert_date) <= '2022-06-30'
  AND country_code_2 IS NOT NULL
  AND country_code_2 <> ''
views.description: All city rows from the cities table whose insert_date falls in June 2022, normalized to a calendar date (time truncated). Exclude rows with NULL or empty country_code_2.

views.name: country_date_presence
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code_2,
  insert_date_date,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS presence,
  MIN(city_id) AS example_city_id
FROM cities_june_2022_dates
GROUP BY country_code_2, insert_date_date
views.description: For each country (country_code_2) and calendar date in June 2022, indicate whether at least one city had an insert on that date. One row per country/date with a boolean or presence marker.

views.name: country_streak_lengths
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cdp.country_code_2 AS country_code_2,
  cdp.insert_date_date AS streak_start_date,
  (
    -- compute length by counting consecutive dates starting at this date for the country
    SELECT COUNT(1)
    FROM country_date_presence c2
    WHERE c2.country_code_2 = cdp.country_code_2
      AND DATE(c2.insert_date_date) >= DATE(cdp.insert_date_date)
      AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM country_date_presence c_missing
        WHERE c_missing.country_code_2 = cdp.country_code_2
          AND DATE(c_missing.insert_date_date) > DATE(cdp.insert_date_date)
          AND DATE(c_missing.insert_date_date) < DATE(c2.insert_date_date)
          AND c_missing.presence = 0
      )
      AND c2.presence = 1
  ) AS streak_length
FROM country_date_presence cdp
WHERE cdp.presence = 1
views.description: For each country, aggregate streak rows into streak-level records and compute the length (number of consecutive days) of each streak.

views.name: cities_countries_january_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code_2,
  country_name,
  created_on
FROM cities_countries
WHERE strftime('%m', created_on) = '01'
views.description: All rows from cities_countries that occur in January of any year (rows where created_on is in January). This produces one row per cities_countries record in January to be used for date-based analyses. Do not apply year-specific filters here.

views.name: country_january_day_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code_2,
  country_name,
  date(substr(created_on, 1, 10)) AS date,
  CASE WHEN created_on IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_row_flag
FROM cities_countries
WHERE strftime('%m', substr(created_on,1,10)) = '01'
views.description: For each country (by country_code_2 and country_name) and calendar date in January, indicate whether there is at least one cities_countries row for that date; used to compute distinct-day counts and to find consecutive-day runs within January.

views.name: cities_date_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  insert_date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_month,
  CAST(strftime('%d', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_day
FROM cities
views.description: Normalize and canonicalize cities rows with parsed date parts from the insert_date column (extract year, month, and day as integers) and keep original primary key. This produces one cleaned row per city with easy-to-filter date fields.

views.name: cities_filtered_by_year_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  city_id,
  insert_date,
  insert_year,
  insert_month
FROM
  cities_date_normalized
WHERE
  insert_year IN (2021, 2022, 2023)
  AND insert_month IN ('April', 'May', 'June')
GROUP BY
  city_id
views.description: Filter normalized cities to only rows whose insert_year is in the set of years relevant for baseline and comparisons (e.g., 2021, 2022, 2023) and whose insert_month is one of April, May, or June. This is a cohort of city rows constrained by date ranges but remains one row per city_id.

views.name: cities_monthly_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER) AS insert_month,
  COUNT(city_id) AS monthly_total
FROM cities
WHERE insert_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', insert_date) AS INTEGER), CAST(strftime('%m', insert_date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregate filtered city rows to produce counts per year and month (one row per combination of insert_year and insert_month) representing the monthly total number of cities inserted in that month/year.

views.name: cities_month_running_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.insert_year,
  m.insert_month,
  m.monthly_total,
  -- running total for this calendar month across years up to and including insert_year
  (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
   FROM cities_monthly_counts AS m2
   WHERE m2.insert_month = m.insert_month
     AND m2.insert_year <= m.insert_year
  ) AS running_total_for_month,
  -- monthly total for same month in prior year (NULL if none)
  (SELECT m_prev.monthly_total
   FROM cities_monthly_counts AS m_prev
   WHERE m_prev.insert_month = m.insert_month
     AND m_prev.insert_year = m.insert_year - 1
   LIMIT 1
  ) AS monthly_total_prev_year,
  -- running total for this calendar month up to prior year (NULL if none)
  (SELECT SUM(m2.monthly_total)
   FROM cities_monthly_counts AS m2
   WHERE m2.insert_month = m.insert_month
     AND m2.insert_year <= m.insert_year - 1
  ) AS running_total_prev_year
FROM cities_monthly_counts AS m
views.description: Compute running totals per calendar month across years: for each (insert_year, insert_month) produce the cumulative sum of monthly_total for that insert_month over all years up to and including insert_year. Also include prior-year values for computing year-over-year comparisons (use LAG over year partitioned by month).

views.name: data_analyst_remote_postings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  jp.job_id,
  jp.job_title_short,
  jp.job_work_from_home,
  jp.salary_year_avg
FROM job_postings_enriched jp
WHERE jp.job_title_short = 'Data Analyst'
  AND jp.job_work_from_home = 1
  AND jp.salary_year_avg IS NOT NULL
views.description: All job_postings_fact rows that are Data Analyst postings, are remote, and have a non-null annual salary. This is a row-level cohort of candidate postings used for downstream skill counting and salary calculations.

views.name: skills_count_for_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.skill_id AS skill_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sj.job_id) AS postings_count
FROM skills_dim s
LEFT JOIN skills_job_dim sj
  ON s.skill_id = sj.skill_id
LEFT JOIN data_analyst_remote_postings dap
  ON sj.job_id = dap.job_id
WHERE dap.job_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.skill_id
views.description: Counts of distinct postings from the Data Analyst remote salary cohort associated with each skill. One row per skill with frequency of associated cohort postings.
